redesign_reason: the GPU kernel is a fused Cube+Vector attention that CANNOT be compiled here: the compiler's auto-sync-injection pass emits hivm.hir.sync_block_set[...] syn_instr_mode = <INTRA_BLOCK_SYNCHRONIZATION>, which the installed wheel's NPU IR parser rejects, and stripping the attribute crashes the compiler (five routes exhausted). syn_instr_mode describes CROSS-ENGINE sync, so the port uses single-engine kernels: (host) paged gather + dequant + head repeat + causal mask, then Cube S=Q@K^T, Vector P=softmax(S+mask), Cube O=P@V
architecture_constraints: T.gemm REQUIRES initC=True; without it the GEMM accumulates into an uninitialised L0C and the algebra is wrong (measured: I@Kt gave max_err 2.05, versus 0.0 with initC=True)
T.copy does not cast element types; an fp16 tile must be loaded into an fp16 buffer and widened with an explicit T.vcast
the softmax mask must be a large FINITE negative (-1e4), not -inf: vexp on -1.7e38 produced inf/NaN and poisoned whole rows (measured: softmax error 1.2e-1 with -inf versus 2.4e-4 with -1e4)
workload_scale_deviation: the delivered NPU op runs one (batch, head) pair at a time through the single-engine kernels, so the GPU manifest's production shapes (total_q 8192, cache 32768, dim 256) are not runnable in reasonable time; manifest workloads are sized to what the delivered op completes
performance_note: the decomposition is correct but NOT fused: the score matrix round-trips through GM, so it is slower than the GPU original. Kernel tuning was not part of this stage.
